subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 29, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 29, 2026

Good morning AcreetionOS community. Today brings several important fixes and improvements across our development pipeline that we are excited to share with you.

Our team resolved a geocode-glib update conflict that was affecting installed systems, ensuring smoother package upgrades for all users. This fix addresses a dependency issue that could cause update failures on existing installations.

Darren has been hard at work on the Calamares installer configuration, removing mandatory disk encryption from the default setup while adding better support for older Nvidia graphics cards. The boot configuration now prefers 1080p gfxmode over native 4K resolution, which should improve compatibility across a wider range of hardware.

On the infrastructure side, Natalie has configured Secret Detection and SAST scanning in our GitLab CI pipelines, strengthening our security posture. The us-infra-hub project received pinned v0.3.0 archive checksums and a new MCP stdio server, while the immutable image build pipeline was fixed to properly handle GitHub releases.

Upstream security updates are rolling in from multiple distributions including AlmaLinux, Debian, and Fedora, covering kernels, Chromium, and various system libraries. Greg Kroah-Hartman also released eight stable kernel versions addressing a single vulnerability, which will flow into our repositories soon.

KDE contributors have delivered notable performance improvements in Dolphin 26.08 and KIO, with Méven Car detailing the optimizations in a two-part blog series. These enhancements should make file operations noticeably snappier for users running our Cinnamon desktop with KDE applications.

The father-daughter development team continues to balance serious engineering with their signature dynamic, as Darren jokes about keeping the server alive after Natalie's weekly production adventures. Their complementary skills in Calamares customization, CI/CD pipelines, and frontend work keep the project moving forward.

For users experiencing boot display issues on high-resolution monitors, the new 1080p gfxmode default should resolve most problems without manual intervention. You can still adjust this in the bootloader configuration if your setup handles native 4K without issues.

Join us on Discord at discord.gg/VHqQkJASw7 to discuss these updates, report any issues, or just chat with fellow AcreetionOS enthusiasts. As always, thank you for being part of our sovereign Arch Linux journey.
